newsitem.title: CHINA: China's Sundiro Motorcycle to buy firms.
newsitem.headline: China's Sundiro Motorcycle to buy firms.

text.p: China's Hainan Sundiro Motorcycle Co Ltd said on Tuesday it planned to acquire a local rubber plant and a motorcycle frame maker.

Sundiro, based in Haikou, capital of the island province of Hainan, said it hoped to purchase a majority stake in Hainan Nongkeng Rubber Plant for cash and acquire Hainan Guanghua Industrial Development Co by assuming its debts.

The Haikou-based company, one of the nation's leading motorcycle makers, told the Hong Kong-based newsletter the China Securities Bulletin that no price had been finalised and that discussions were under way.

The rubber plant's total assets were valued at 181.11 million yuan ($21.8 million) at the end of June 1997, against total liabilities of 119.28 million, Sundiro said in a statement published in the Shenzhen-based Securities Times.
The total assets of Guanghua, a motorcycle frame producer, were valued at 34.64 million yuan on April 30, 1997, against total liabilities of 41.51 million, it said.
Sundiro is preparing an initial public offering of 150 million hard currency B shares to be listed in Shenzhen.
A Sundiro spokesman said the company hopes to have an agreement reached by October, ahead of the B share offering.
The acquisition requires approval of shareholders at a forthcoming meeting, Sundiro said without giving further details.
Sundiro has said it would use part of the B share proceeds to upgrade production technology and set up a venture with Japanese firm Kawasaki to make motorbike engines.
It would use the remaining money to finance the acquisition of a 60 percent stake in Hainan Automotive Factory and turn it into a limited company with registered capital of 700 million yuan.
Hainan Automotive factory has been negotiating with Daimler-Benz AG's Mercedes-Benz arm to build multi-purpose vans, Sundiro officials have said.
They said Sundiro planned to issue an additional 20 million B shares if the first-tranche offer was oversubscribed.
Sundiro posted net profits of 219 million yuan in 1996 against 70.55 million yuan in 1995 based on Chinese accounting standards.
Sundiro, one of the 33 companies selected by Beijing to issue B shares, has a production target of 600,000 to 800,000 motorcycles this year.
At the end of 1996, Sundiro had about 237 million outstanding shares, composed of 142 million institutional shares, 95 million A shares and 72,240 staff shares.
